package middleware

import (
	"net/http"
	"net/http/httptest"
	"testing"

	"github.com/labstack/echo/v4"
	"github.com/stretchr/testify/assert"
)

func TestTmpProxyBalancerWithNoTargets(t *testing.T) {
	// round robin
	rrb := NewRoundRobinBalancer([]*ProxyTarget{})
	e := echo.New()
	e.Use(Proxy(rrb))
	req := httptest.NewRequest(http.MethodGet, "/", nil)
	rec := httptest.NewRecorder()
	e.ServeHTTP(rec, req)
	assert.Equal(t, http.StatusServiceUnavailable, rec.Code)

	// random
	rb := NewRandomBalancer(nil)
	e = echo.New()
	e.Use(Proxy(rb))
	rec = httptest.NewRecorder()
	e.ServeHTTP(rec, req)
	assert.Equal(t, http.StatusServiceUnavailable, rec.Code)

	// targets removed after start
	rrb2 := NewRoundRobinBalancer([]*ProxyTarget{{Name: "t", URL: req.URL}})
	assert.True(t, rrb2.RemoveTarget("t"))
	e = echo.New()
	e.Use(Proxy(rrb2))
	rec = httptest.NewRecorder()
	e.ServeHTTP(rec, req)
	assert.Equal(t, http.StatusServiceUnavailable, rec.Code)
}
EOF

arguments.text: Done: empty responses no longer leak a 10-byte gzip header into the body. `gzipResponseWriter.Write` now returns early for zero-length writes, so an empty body stays empty (and no bogus Content-Type is sniffed) while Content-Encoding is dropped for empty responses. Full suite still green.

Done: map binding now supports map[string][]string. `bindData` delegates map destinations to a new `bindDataToMap`, which binds the whole []string slice when the map element type is a slice and the first value otherwise (map[string]string / map[string]interface{} behaviour unchanged). Verified: map[string][]string{"foo":{"bar","baz"}} binds correctly, no panic; full suite green.

Done: `context.Scheme()` now only honours valid scheme values — X-Forwarded-Proto / X-Forwarded-Protocol / X-Url-Scheme are used only when they are exactly "http" or "https" (X-Forwarded-Ssl only when "on"), otherwise it falls back to "http". Invalid headers are ignored as the doc contract (returns "http" or "https") requires.

Done: `ProxyWithConfig` now returns `echo.ErrServiceUnavailable` (503) instead of panicking when the balancer has no targets; both `randomBalancer.Next` and `roundRobinBalancer.Next` return nil for an empty target list (previously rand.Intn(0) / modulo-by-zero panics).
